card.questionText: Explain, with the aid of notes and freehand sketches, any five of the following: triple glazing; wind turbine; carbon monoxide alarm; mortise and tenon joint; butt hinge; ball valve; cordless circular saw; fascia board; smart meter.

rows.contextNote: Explain any five of the nine terms. Each term is marked separately: primary communication of relevant information 6 and other communication 4, in notes or sketches (the scheme reserves no fixed split between them). Triple glazing: three panes of glass separated by insulating gaps, often argon-filled; more energy efficient than single or double glazing; high thermal and sound insulation; typically dearer than double glazing. Wind turbine: converts the kinetic energy of wind into electricity; renewable, emission-free generation; on land or offshore, singly or in wind farms; Ireland produces a large share of its energy from wind. Carbon monoxide alarm: detects carbon monoxide, a colourless, odourless, poisonous gas from fuel-burning appliances (boilers, stoves, fires, heaters), and sounds a warning; mandatory when installing new or replacement fossil-fuel appliances; test it regularly. Mortise and tenon joint: a tenon cut on the end of one piece fits a mortise cut in the other; very strong with a large gluing area; used for chair and table legs and rails, doors and windows; a stopped joint hides the tenon. Butt hinge: a common hinge joining a door to its frame; two rectangular leaves joined by knuckles and a pin; the leaves sit flush when the door closes; for interior or exterior doors, cabinets and lids; strong and affordable. Ball valve: controls flow with a rotating ball with a hole through it; open when the hole lines up with the pipe, closed when it is at right angles; the handle shows open, closed or partly open; used to isolate plumbing for maintenance or emergencies. Cordless circular saw: a portable battery-powered (usually lithium-ion) saw for cutting wood, and sometimes metal or plastic, without a mains cable; can make rip, cross and bevel cuts. Fascia board: a horizontal board fixed to the ends of the rafters along the lower edge of the roof; timber or uPVC; protects the rafter ends and supports the gutter; closes the roof against moisture and pests; available in colours and decorative profiles. Smart meter: an electricity meter that records use automatically and sends readings to the supplier, ending manual and estimated readings; splits use into day, night and peak times; shows usage patterns to help choose a tariff and save energy.
